answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by pricing reputation through verifiable work, not identity. Standing is earned only by completing attested tasks, kept in a shared orchard of endorsements that grows slowly and fades when idle. A newcomer must first take small, supervised jobs, so spawning a hundred fake identities means a hundred streams of work first. Like a river deepening its channel, trust accumulates gradually: a Sybil operator must pay the full cost of labor for every fake agent, while the nectar of high-value work stays reserved for agents whose record proves honest effort.
